title: Moving Company CRM: Six Tools That Speed Up Lead Follow-Up
html:
A moving company CRM should log every quote request, remind your team to follow up and show which leads became booked moves. Most movers choose between a moving-specific platform such as SmartMoving or MoverBase and a general CRM such as HubSpot. Feed it with steady lead generation so the pipeline always has quotes to work. Published plans in this guide run from free to $299 a month, and two vendors publish no price.

A moving company CRM has to do three jobs: capture every lead, reply fast and keep the quote moving until the customer books. A move is a one-time sale, and the customer often asks several movers for a price. The company that follows up first and clearest has the advantage.

This guide sorts six tools by the job each one does, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Which moving company CRM is built into moving software?

SmartMoving, MoverBase and Granot all fold customer records and lead handling into software built for movers. That saves you from linking a CRM to a quoting tool later.

Two of these three hide the price. Ask each for a written quote at your seat count and job volume. Compare it with MoverBase, which publishes every plan.

Speed to lead is a metric you can test. During the demo, send a test lead through the website form and time how long it takes to reach a person. If the tool cannot show that time, you cannot manage it.

Which free CRM works for a moving company that already has a quoting tool?

HubSpot CRM is the free pick for a mover that wants a sales pipeline and email tools beside an existing estimate app. It does not know what a move is, so every move field is one you add.

  • HubSpot CRM: a general sales CRM that lists up to 1,000 contacts and one-to-one email on its Free plan. The Free plan is $0 for up to 2 users with no credit card. Starter starts at $7 per seat a month on annual billing, and the page's FAQ states $10 per seat month to month. Limit: the free plan caps at 2 users, and the page shows two Starter figures, so confirm the one you will pay.

Add fields for the move date, origin city, destination city and home size. Then build one pipeline with stages such as new, estimate booked, quote sent and booked. A deal that sits in quote sent for too long shows you where to call.

A free CRM is also the cheapest way to learn what you need. Run it for a month, then see which reports you used. That tells you whether a moving-specific tool is worth its price.

A small crew with one owner and one estimator can run well on this. A team with several salespeople needs the pipeline add-on or a separate CRM, so price both before you pick.

Which free tool sends leads into the CRM?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows a moving company in Google Maps and local search. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, photos, reviews and phone number when someone searches for movers nearby. Limit: it needs current photos, posts and review replies, and it does not track the lead after the call.

See Google's Business Profile help page for setup. Every call from the listing is a lead the CRM must capture, so log the source on each one.

How do you choose a moving company CRM?

Choose a moving company CRM with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it capture leads from your website, phone and lead providers, flag duplicates and send email and text follow-up?

Cost: count users, job caps, extra-job fees and contract length, then compare the total against what one booked move earns you.

Setup effort: can one person connect the website form and build the pipeline in a week, or does the vendor need to do it?

A one-estimator mover can run HubSpot CRM beside MoverBase Mover Pro, plus a free Google Business Profile. A multi-crew company with a sales team fits SmartMoving or Granot, once a written quote beats what the team loses in slow replies.

Test the reports before you sign. Ask to see leads by source, quotes by status and booked moves by month. If the vendor cannot show those three views from sample data, you will build them by hand every week. That time can outweigh the plan price.

Keep the contract term in view. SmartMoving lists 12, 24 and 36-month subscriptions, so a wrong pick costs a year or more. A month-to-month tool such as MoverBase or HubSpot lets you change your mind.

How should a moving company follow up a new lead?

Reply to a new moving lead within minutes during business hours, and write down who owns the reply. A customer comparing movers often books the first clear quote.

  • Call, then text: a missed call gets a text with your name and a link to book an estimate.
  • Send the quote in writing: include the date, crew size and what is covered, so the customer can compare.
  • Set a second touch: every open quote gets a reminder date, so a quiet lead gets one more contact.
  • Ask about flexibility: a customer with a flexible date may take a slow day at a better fit.
  • Close the loop: mark each lead booked or lost, with a reason, so you learn from the lost ones.

The same rules apply to every source. A lead from a map listing, a search ad or a lead provider should enter one pipeline with one owner.

What email and text automation should a moving CRM send?

A moving CRM should send a confirmation right after the lead arrives, a reminder before the estimate and a follow-up after the quote. Three messages cover most of the work.

  • Instant confirmation: thank the customer, state your name and say when someone will call.
  • Estimate reminder: send a text the day before a virtual or on-site estimate.
  • Quote follow-up: send a short email two days after the quote with a link to book.
  • Review request: after the move, ask for a review while the experience is fresh.

SmartMoving and Granot both list automated email and text. MoverBase lists the embedded website form and integrations only on paid plans. Check which messages each plan includes before you count on them.

Keep the tone plain. A short message from a named person beats a long template. Never send more than one follow-up a day.

What should a moving CRM track on every lead?

A moving CRM should track the lead source, move date, origin, destination, home size and quote status on every lead. These fields decide who calls first and what you quote.

  • Lead source: record whether the lead came from your website, a map listing, a search ad, a referral or a lead provider. This is the field that shows where marketing money works.
  • Move date and flexibility: a move in ten days outranks a move in three months, so sort the list by date.
  • Origin and destination: distance changes the quote and the crew plan.
  • Quote status and value: mark each lead new, estimate booked, quote sent, booked or lost, and enter the quote amount.
  • Next step and date: every open lead needs one action and a due date.

Keep the form short. A sales rep who must fill twelve fields skips them, and then the reports are empty.

How do lead providers fit into a moving CRM?

Lead providers should feed the CRM directly, so a purchased lead gets the same reply rules as a website lead. Sending them to a personal inbox slows the first reply.

  • SmartMoving: the page says website forms and lead providers can send leads in through its Lead API, and that it flags duplicates.
  • MoverBase: paid plans list 15+ lead providers, while the Free plan does not.
  • Granot: the site lists an API for receiving moving leads and automation that reacts to incoming leads.

Duplicates are a real cost. A customer who fills in three provider forms creates three leads, and three calls annoy them. A tool that flags duplicates, as SmartMoving lists, protects the first impression.

Track each provider's booked rate separately. A provider that sends many leads but few bookings looks cheap on a per-lead basis and expensive per move.

How do you bring more moving leads into the CRM?

A CRM only works the leads it receives. Search ads put your company in front of people about to move.

For more ideas, read the lead generation tips , PPC management tips , Meta Ads tips and web design tips for moving companies.

If a bad review lands, read how to answer a negative review before you reply.

What is the best CRM for a moving company?

There is no single best pick. SmartMoving, MoverBase and Granot build lead handling into moving software, HubSpot CRM is free for up to 2 users, and Jobber suits a small crew. Test each one by sending a lead through it and timing the reply.

How much does a moving company CRM cost?

Published plans in this guide run from free for HubSpot CRM and MoverBase to $299 a month for MoverBase Unlimited. Jobber Core lists at $49 a month with no commitment. SmartMoving and Granot publish no price, so request a written quote before you compare.

Does a moving company need a CRM and moving software?

Not always. Moving platforms such as SmartMoving and MoverBase include customer records and lead tools, so one system can do both jobs. Add a separate CRM such as HubSpot only when your quoting tool lacks the pipeline and email features you need.

Is HubSpot CRM free for movers?

Yes, for a small team. HubSpot lists a Free plan at $0 for up to 2 users with no credit card required. It lists up to 1,000 contacts and one-to-one email. It has no move, truck or crew features, so pair it with a quoting and scheduling tool.

What should a moving CRM track on each lead?

Track the lead source, move date, origin and destination, home size, quote status and next follow-up date. The lead source shows which channel pays you, and the follow-up date keeps a quiet quote from going cold before the customer books.

How fast should a moving company reply to a quote request?

Reply within minutes during business hours when you can, and the same day at the latest. Customers often ask several movers for a price, and the first clear written quote often wins the booking. Assign one person to own every first reply.

Does a moving CRM send automatic emails and texts?

SmartMoving lists automated email and text follow-up, and Granot lists automated emails and tasks plus two-way texting. HubSpot lists one-to-one email on its Free plan, with HubSpot branding. Confirm which plan includes the messages you want, because pages often limit them to higher tiers.
